meta.name: Hive
meta.tagline: Tu colmena de agentes IA. Local-first. Multi-canal. Open source. Construido desde Colombia para el mundo.
meta.product_type: Agent Harness — per README's own positioning: pre-built operational infrastructure around an LLM (tools, memory, error handling, deployment, observability), explicitly NOT an agent framework (contrasted against LangChain/CrewAI/AutoGen in docs/HIVE-HARNESS.md). 'Runtime' in this document refers to packages/core specifically (the engine inside the harness), not a claim that Hive is 'just a runtime'.

Confirmed by source (zero bun:sqlite/better-sqlite3 usage left in packages/core/src) — note that README.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/HIVE-HARNESS.md still describe the store as SQLite (data/hive.db); those docs predate the HiveDB migration and are stale on this point.

specialist_hive.summary: One coordinator remains the only user-facing agent. Specialists are dormant, typed templates in HiveDB and consume no model or MCP resources until a routed task wakes them. The free worker remains the fallback for rare tasks.
specialist_hive.routing: The coordinator resolves simple requests itself. For complex work it emits bounded subtasks with minimal context, explicit acceptance criteria and a suggested loadout. Active specialists are retrieved by BM25/hybrid search over their routing descriptions.
specialist_hive.verification_gate: Every delegated or effectful delivery is evaluated by acceptance_verifier, which is independent from the executing specialist. Missing evidence, unmet criteria or malformed output fail closed; the coordinator cannot report success until a passing VerificationDoc exists.
specialist_hive.lifecycle: select → materialize prompt/tools/skills/model → connect allowlisted MCP lazily → execute → independently verify → persist proof and ACE trace → hibernate → disconnect MCP after TTL

catalog.description: Investiga preguntas actuales en fuentes web y entrega conclusiones verificables con referencias.
Navega sitios, completa formularios y verifica visualmente el estado final de una operación web.
Crea, lee, edita, organiza y elimina archivos o carpetas dentro del workspace autorizado.
Implementa, depura y prueba software dentro de un repositorio o workspace existente.
Lee y genera documentos PDF, Word, Excel y PowerPoint dentro del workspace.
Presenta resultados, listas, tarjetas y progreso mediante el Canvas clásico.
Construye formularios, dashboards y flujos interactivos compatibles con A2UI v0.9.
Crea y administra recordatorios y automatizaciones temporales con zona horaria correcta.
Registra reuniones y genera informes con decisiones, responsables y próximos pasos.
Transcribe audio y genera respuestas habladas mediante proveedores STT y TTS.
Ejecuta y verifica operaciones contra APIs REST expresamente autorizadas.
Opera herramientas de servicios externos descubiertas mediante MCP y verifica sus efectos.
Verifica de forma independiente que una tarea cumplió todos sus criterios antes de autorizar que el principal reporte éxito.

persistence.specialists: Typed specialist templates, routing text, loadouts, workspace/model policy, acceptance defaults, active flag and ACE counters.
persistence.verifications: Per-run verdict, criterion-level evidence, risks and verifier identity.
persistence.specialistProposals: Curator proposals to move tools, create recurring specialities or disable harmful specialists.
persistence.attribution: specialist_id on agents, runs, tasks, traces and proof packets feeds per-speciality playbooks and health metrics.

specialist_hive.parallelism: Different specialists may run in parallel on independent durable-queue lanes. Repeated tasks for the same specialist reuse its stable warm context when scope and loadout match.

runtime_flow.description: CLI (`hive start` / `hive dev`) launches the gateway: gateway/server.ts's startGateway().

Gateway boots HiveDB storage, ChannelManager, AgentService+AgentRunner, the durable queue + job executors, CronScheduler + DAGScheduler + task-driver, canvasManager, and the voice/multimodal services.
Gateway registers ~20 REST route modules and serves the pre-built hive-ui SPA.
Inbound channel messages, webchat turns, and cron/DAG triggers become jobs (chat_turn, goal_run, project_task, worker_task) on the durable queue.

The coordinator resolves simple work itself; otherwise it retrieves an active specialist by task description and delegates a bounded subtask with minimal context and explicit acceptance criteria. The free worker remains the fallback when no specialist fits.

specialist-runtime materializes the selected dormant template with its exact system prompt, tool allowlist, skills and model policy, then lazily connects only its authorized MCP servers. agent-loop executes it through the normal Native Agent Loop.
run-store checkpoints/leases each run in HiveDB; job-store/durable-queue do the same for jobs with idempotency keys and logical-failure retry with backoff, separate from crash recovery.

acceptance_verifier independently evaluates every criterion against evidence and persists a VerificationDoc. Failure or insufficient evidence returns to execution; only a passing verification authorizes success.
proof-packet + run-epoch record the verified outcome and its provider/model/tool-catalog epoch. Traces attributed by specialist_id update its ACE playbook and health counters.
The coordinator—not the specialist—reports the verified result to the originating channel. The specialist hibernates and lazy MCP connections are released after TTL.

docs.summary: Defines 'tool legibility' conventions for tools/ and tool-runtime/, based on the harness-engineering discover→select→invoke→interpret→verify practice: (a) dry-run mode (dryRun?: boolean) for any tool with side effects, (b) bounded/stable output shapes (truncate, avoid data: any), (c) stable structured failure signatures ({code, message, hint}) so job-executors.ts can classify retryability via resilience/retry.ts#isRetryableError.
